SUMMARY: Loan repayment never auto-picks a loan
USER_STORY: As a user with two or more loans, I want the repayment form to open with no loan chosen, so I never record a payment against an arbitrary debt without noticing.
DESCRIPTION: TransactionForm.tsx:272-275 [5b] add-transaction-spec Section2, README Part 1 #3 (High severity, data integrity). A useEffect calls handleLoanChange(loanAccounts[0].id) whenever the form is in repayment mode with no loan selected. handleLoanChange (line 215) also overwrites currency, account_id and description, so with 2+ loans the form opens pre-filled against the first loan and an unnoticed submit records a financially wrong entry. Not covered by any Epic 0-7 ticket and not mentioned in any retro: the audit said 'ship these first' but tickets.md never cut a ticket for it. Fix: only the single-loan case auto-selects. Put the rule in a pure helper resolveInitialLoanId(loans, lockedLoanAccountId, editTarget) in src/lib/loanPicker.ts (relative imports only, per AGENTS.md) with a node --test file, and call it from the effect. With 2+ loans to_account_id stays null and the existing 'Choose the loan you are repaying' error blocks submit; until LED-105 adds the picker step the existing 'Loan to repay' Select is the only way to choose. Related, decided in LED-113: the card-payment effect at lines 266-269 also picks cardAccounts.find(balance < 0) ?? cardAccounts[0]. TransactionForm is a god node (degree 35): keep the diff to the effect and the helper. Ships alone in Phase 1.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) With exactly one loan the form opens with that loan selected; (b) with 2+ loans it opens with to_account_id null and currency, account_id and description untouched until the user picks a loan, and Submit shows 'Choose the loan you are repaying'; (c) with lockedLoanAccountId the loan is selected and the field stays disabled regardless of loan count; (d) editing a saved repayment (editTarget 'loan') still opens on its own loan; (e) resolveInitialLoanId is unit-tested for 0, 1 and 2+ loans, locked and editing; (f) lint, build and test pass.

USER_STORY: As a user with two or more loans, I want to choose which loan I am repaying from a list that shows what I owe and what is due, so I never have to guess from a bare name.
DESCRIPTION: TransactionForm.tsx, a new LoanPicker component in src/components/transactions, src/lib/loanPicker.ts [5a, 5b] add-transaction-spec Section2. With 2+ loans the dialog opens a picker step first and the form is unreachable until a loan is chosen. One row per loan account: name; formatLoanSchedule(account) (src/lib/loans.ts) as the secondary line; outstanding from getLoanAmountOwed(account); next deadline from getLoanDeadlines(purchases, allocations) (src/lib/loanInstallments.ts), the amount and date of the installment falling in the current cycle when there is one. Rows sort by nearest due date, then largest outstanding (pure sortLoanChoices in loanPicker.ts, tested). Choosing a row runs the existing handleLoanChange and advances; Back from the form returns to the picker with the selection intact. Follow the two-step pattern already in LoanPurchaseForm.tsx (advanceToRepayment, the Purchase / Repayment stepper) so the flows feel the same. useLoanPurchases(accountId) reads one account, so the picker needs one batched read of purchases and allocations for all loan accounts, not one hook per row; a failed read goes through resolveLoadState and shows the error state, never an empty list (AGENTS.md). A single loan or lockedLoanAccountId skips the picker. Focus moves to the picker heading on open (LED-91 rule, knowledge/patterns/dialog-focus.md). Depends on LED-104.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) With 2+ loans choosing 'Loan repayment' opens the picker first and the form cannot be reached until a loan is chosen; (b) each row shows name, schedule, outstanding and, when one falls in the current cycle, the next deadline amount and date; (c) rows sort by nearest due date then largest outstanding, covered by a unit test; (d) choosing a row calls handleLoanChange and advances, and Back returns to the picker with that row still selected; (e) one loan, or a locked loan (entering from a loan account page), skips the picker; (f) a failed purchases read shows an error state with retry, not blank rows; (g) focus lands on the picker heading and returns to the trigger on close; (h) lint, build and test pass.

SUMMARY: Repayment summary band and amount presets
USER_STORY: As a user recording a loan repayment, I want to see what is outstanding, what is due and what my balance will be after this payment, so I stop discovering the limits as validation errors.
DESCRIPTION: TransactionForm.tsx, src/lib/loanRepayment.ts [5b] add-transaction-spec Section3.2 and 3.3. Three read-only figures directly under the loan field, recomputed as the loan or amount changes: Outstanding = getLoanAmountOwed(selectedLoan); Installment due = nearest getLoanDeadlines entry in the current cycle (amount, date, 'in N days'); After this payment = outstanding - amount with the installment count stepping (34 of 48 -> 35 of 48). Amount presets: Installment (default when a deadline exists in the cycle, sets the amount to that installment total), Pay in full (sets getLoanAmountOwed via roundMoney from loanInstallments.ts so it can never trip the cap by a cent), Custom (leaves the field as typed). With no deadline in the cycle default to Custom with an empty amount. 'After this payment' must never render negative: when the amount exceeds outstanding show the existing error 'Payment cannot exceed the outstanding loan amount' instead. All existing validation and messages stay exactly as written (Section 3.1). The card form already has a stats band (the dl near TransactionForm.tsx:385, LED-24): reuse its markup and tokens, do not fork a second band. Compute in a pure summariseRepayment(loan, deadlines, amount) in src/lib/loanRepayment.ts with node --test coverage. Depends on LED-105.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) The three figures render under the loan field and update as the amount is typed; (b) Installment due shows amount, date and days until, and is absent with a stated reason when no deadline falls in the cycle; (c) After this payment never shows a negative figure, the existing over-outstanding error shows instead; (d) Installment is the default preset when a deadline exists, otherwise Custom with an empty amount; (e) Pay in full equals getLoanAmountOwed and saving it succeeds (rounding test at a cent boundary); (f) summariseRepayment is unit-tested for a deadline, no deadline, over-payment and pay-in-full; (g) existing repayment validation messages are unchanged; (h) lint, build and test pass.

USER_STORY: As a user recording a loan repayment, I want to see how this payment will be applied to each financed purchase before I save it, so the split is not a surprise afterwards.
DESCRIPTION: TransactionForm.tsx, src/lib/loanRepayment.ts [5b] add-transaction-spec Section3.4. useLoanPurchases(accountId) already returns purchases and allocations and LoanPurchaseTracker says 'Repayments will show how much was applied to each purchase' in the past tense; show it before saving. One row per financed purchase: name, 'Installment {paid + 1} of {term}', the amount this payment applies, and the remaining balance after. Split oldest-installment-first, the same order the write path uses when it creates loan_payment_allocations. Reuse getPurchaseInstallments and enrichLoanPurchase (src/lib/loanInstallments.ts); do not reimplement the split and do not let the preview and the saved allocations diverge. Hide the whole block when the loan has no itemised purchases (the unitemised case LED-82 warns about). Read knowledge/rules/loan-payment-date-decides-its-split.md first: allocate_loan_payment splits by what is due on the transaction date, so a payment dated before a due date falls through to a split by remaining balance ($488/$132 instead of $480/$140, LED-83 retro). The preview must take the form's Date field as an input, not 'today'. The SQL function cannot run under node --test, so pin parity with fixtures taken from the LED-83 retro and from a local-database run of the same payments. Depends on LED-106.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) One preview row per financed purchase shows installment N of M, the amount applied and the remaining balance; (b) the split is oldest-installment-first and changes when the Date field changes across a due date; (c) the preview equals the loan_payment_allocations rows written on save, purchase for purchase, for the LED-83 fixtures ($480/$140 on the due date, $488/$132 before it) and for a local-database run; (d) the block is hidden for a loan with no itemised purchases; (e) the preview reuses getPurchaseInstallments and enrichLoanPurchase, with no second split implementation; (f) lint, build and test pass.

SUMMARY: Kind menu: Liabilities group, live descriptions, gold loan tile
USER_STORY: As a user opening Add transaction, I want the menu to group liabilities and show what I owe, so the loan and card actions tell me their state before I pick one.
DESCRIPTION: TransactionKindMenu.tsx, a new src/lib/kindMenu.ts [5a] add-transaction-spec Section1.1 and 1.2. Today the menu has one label ('What would you like to record?'), a bare separator and static descriptions at w-72 (TransactionKindMenu.tsx:64-66). Add a labelled 'Liabilities' group (same kicker style) holding Loan repayment and Card payment; widen to w-80. Descriptions become live: Loan repayment = '{n} loan(s) - {total} owed' from summarizeBalances (src/lib/creditCards.ts, totalLoanDebt), Card payment = the card with the nearest due date, or '{n} cards - {total} due' (totalCreditCardDebt). The Loan repayment tile uses the loan accent var(--gold) on a tinted ground, not bg-primary/10, matching constants/accounts.ts; the Card payment icon is text-expense. Build the item list as data in src/lib/kindMenu.ts (kindMenuItems(accounts, options)) with node --test coverage so LED-109's bottom sheet consumes the same list and the two surfaces cannot drift. Depends on LED-115: there is no gold token until it ships, and GOLD currently resolves to indigo (see Epic 9). TransactionKindMenu has graphify degree 10; AppLayout (22) and TopBar mount it.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) A 'Liabilities' label separates Loan repayment and Card payment from the three primary kinds; (b) descriptions show live counts and totals, and 'n cards' plural handling is tested; (c) the Loan repayment tile uses var(--gold) in light and dark, the Card payment icon uses the expense token; (d) the menu is w-80 and no description wraps at 1280; (e) hasLoans and hasCardBalance visibility rules are unchanged; (f) items come from kindMenuItems and are unit-tested; (g) lint, build and test pass.

SUMMARY: Kind menu as a bottom sheet below md
USER_STORY: As a phone user tapping the add button, I want the kind menu to open as a full-width bottom sheet, not a 288px panel wedged over the bottom nav.
DESCRIPTION: TransactionKindMenu.tsx, AppLayout.tsx [5a mobile frames] add-transaction-spec Section1.4. On mobile the trigger is the corner FAB, so the Radix DropdownMenu renders as a 288px panel pinned bottom-right overlapping the bottom nav with every description wrapping to two lines. Swap the surface below md and keep the dropdown above it. Reuse ui/sheet.tsx with side='bottom' (the mobile More sheet already does this). Drag handle, then 'What would you like to record?' as a 17px sheet title, rows full width with min-height 64px, 44px icon tile, description on one line, trailing chevron. The Liabilities separator becomes an 8px ground-coloured band rather than a 1px rule. Same five items, same order, same strings, fed by kindMenuItems from LED-108. No E / I / T key caps here (desktop only, LED-110). Use useMediaQuery, not a second component tree per breakpoint. Focus moves to the sheet heading on open and returns to the FAB on close (LED-91). Depends on LED-108.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Below md the menu is a bottom sheet with a drag handle, title, 64px rows and a trailing chevron; (b) at md and above it is the dropdown; (c) both surfaces are fed by one item list and a test asserts the two render the same ids in the same order; (d) no key caps in the sheet; (e) descriptions fit on one line at 390 wide; (f) focus moves to the heading on open and back to the FAB on close; (g) lint, build and test pass.

SUMMARY: E / I / T key caps on the kind menu
USER_STORY: As a keyboard user, I want E, I and T to pick Expense, Income and Transfer while the kind menu is open, so adding a transaction is one chord.
DESCRIPTION: TransactionKindMenu.tsx, src/lib/kindMenu.ts [5a] add-transaction-spec Section1.5. E / I / T on the three primary kinds, rendered as a right-aligned key cap; loan repayment and card payment get no letter because they open a second step. Wire as DropdownMenuItem shortcuts that select the item (open the dialog), not merely move focus: Radix typeahead already focuses an item whose label starts with the typed letter, and Expense, Income and Transfer start with E, I and T, so the key must fire the selection. Keep the mapping in one KIND_SHORTCUTS constant in src/lib/kindMenu.ts. This closes the LED-40 deviation: LED-40's Actions 'reuse the E / I / T keys from the kind menu' but the menu had none (LED-40 retro: TransactionKindMenu has no key bindings, spec 1.5 unbuilt). The palette's own gating stays as LED-40 decided (E / I / T fire only after arrowing onto an Actions row, so a search starting with e, i or t is not hijacked); only the mapping is shared. Hidden in the mobile sheet. Depends on LED-108.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) The three primary kinds show E, I and T key caps in the dropdown; (b) pressing the key while the menu is open opens the matching dialog (a test or scripted browser check proves selection, not just focus); (c) Loan repayment and Card payment have no letter; (d) the SearchPalette Actions group reads the same KIND_SHORTCUTS constant; (e) no key caps on the bottom sheet; (f) lint, build and test pass.

SUMMARY: New-transaction dialog states its kind, with Change kind
USER_STORY: As a user who just picked a kind, I want the dialog to name it once and let me change it, so I am not asked the same question twice and a mis-pick is not a dead end.
DESCRIPTION: TransactionForm.tsx, AppLayout.tsx:230-235 [4c, 5b, 12a] add-transaction-spec Section3.5 (creating), README Part 1 #17. TransactionKindMenu already collects the kind. The kind becomes the dialog's identity: a tinted icon tile plus TRANSACTION_KIND_LABELS[kind] as the title ('New expense', 'New income', 'New transfer'), the menu's own description as the subtitle (reuse the strings from kindMenuItems, LED-108, do not write new ones), and a required 'Change kind' link in the header that reopens TransactionKindMenu with the chosen kind still highlighted. Loan repayment and card payment state their kind in the title and offer no selector (5b, 12a). Evidence today: TransactionForm has no type control at all (the only writes are form.setValue('type', 'expense') at lines 229 and 255), so the 'remove the selector' half of the spec is already true and this ticket is the identity and the Change kind link; the title comes from AppLayout via TRANSACTION_KIND_DIALOG_TITLES. The mobile add sheet (LED-103) must carry the same header. TransactionForm (degree 35) and AppLayout (22) are god nodes. Depends on LED-108 and LED-109.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Choosing Expense opens a dialog titled 'New expense' with a tinted tile and the menu subtitle, and no type selector; (b) 'Change kind' returns to the menu with the chosen kind still highlighted and choosing another kind swaps the form without losing entered shared fields (amount, date, description); (c) loan repayment and card payment titles state the kind and show no Change kind link to a different form family unless it is safe (record the decision); (d) the same header renders in the mobile add sheet at 390 wide; (e) lint, build and test pass.

SUMMARY: Edit mode Kind selector that clears fields that no longer apply
USER_STORY: As a user fixing a mistyped entry, I want to change an expense into a transfer while editing, so I do not have to delete it and record it again.
DESCRIPTION: TransactionForm.tsx (isEditing), a new src/lib/transactionKindChange.ts [4c] add-transaction-spec Section3.5 (editing), README Part 1 #17. Today no control changes a saved transaction's kind, so the only route to fix a mistyped entry is delete and re-record. In edit mode show a 'Kind' selector as the first control, set to the row's current type. Changing kind must clear the fields that no longer apply rather than letting transactionFormSchema reject on submit: a transfer has no category_id or subcategory, an expense has no to_account_id. Put the clearing in a pure applyKindChange(values, nextKind) in src/lib/transactionKindChange.ts (relative imports only) with node --test coverage. Saved loan repayments and card payments (editTarget 'loan' or 'card', inferred by inferTransactionKind from the target account type) show their kind as fixed text in the title, with no selector; the selector offers expense, income and transfer only. Cross-currency: switching to a transfer between accounts of different currencies must ask for the rate through the existing exchange-rate field, not fail on submit. Independent of the create-mode work, so it can start early.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Editing an expense shows a Kind selector set to Expense; (b) switching expense -> transfer clears category and subcategory and asks for a destination account with no submit-time error; (c) switching transfer -> expense clears to_account_id; (d) a saved loan repayment or card payment shows no selector and states its kind in the title; (e) applyKindChange is unit-tested for every pair of income, expense and transfer; (f) a saved row still infers its kind through inferTransactionKind after a change; (g) lint, build and test pass.

SUMMARY: Card payment 12a layout at three sizes
USER_STORY: As a user paying a credit card, I want the payment form to match the designed layout and wording at desktop, tablet and phone, so the numbers that matter are where the design puts them.
DESCRIPTION: TransactionForm.tsx, AppLayout.tsx [12a] LED-24 retro (acceptance 'built at all three sizes' was recorded PARTIAL). Not built per the LED-24 retro: the 720px desktop modal (the form uses the existing stacked layout in a max-w-md dialog), the three-cell band at tablet, the mobile wording ('Owed now', 'Due Oct 1 in 21d'), and dates in the statement and due copy (the form shows 'day N' plus days until). Also from that retro: the stats band is hidden when the form opens with a prefilled amount (edit or template) because the stored balance already includes it. Decide and record: the card auto-pick at TransactionForm.tsx:266-269 chooses cardAccounts.find(balance < 0) ?? cardAccounts[0]; check against 12a whether a preselected card is drawn and, if not, apply the LED-104 rule (no silent pick with 2+ owing cards). The 12a caption also draws category 'Card payments' and 'Excluded from spending reports'; that is LED-114 and is blocked on OD-2, so this ticket leaves Uncategorized in place. Depends on LED-111 for the shared header.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Desktop renders the 12a modal width and layout; (b) tablet renders the three-cell band; (c) mobile uses the drawn wording and shows real statement and due dates; (d) the stats band behaviour for prefilled amounts is decided and documented in the retro; (e) the multi-card auto-pick is decided against 12a and recorded; (f) checked at 1920x1080, 768x1024 and 390x844 in light and dark; (g) lint, build and test pass.

SUMMARY: Card payments category, excluded from spending reports
USER_STORY: As a user who pays a card, I want the payment to stop counting as spending, so reports and budgets do not count the same purchase twice.
DESCRIPTION: DECIDED 2026-09-26 - OD-2 (b): no Card payments category and no migration. src/lib/cardPayment.ts, src/components/transactions/TransactionForm.tsx [12a] LED-24 retro. Since LED-146 a card payment is saved as a transfer into the card (knowledge/rules/card-payment-is-a-transfer.md), and every spending predicate already filters type = 'expense' (categoryBreakdown.ts, utils.ts topCategories, useBudgets.ts, budgetImpact.ts), so card payments are already excluded from spending totals, the category breakdown, Overspending and budget spend. The ticket's original premise (card payments are counted today) is stale. What remains: (1) one exported predicate isCardPayment in src/lib/cardPayment.ts; (2) a regression test that a transfer into a credit card adds 0 to every spending calculation while a loan repayment (an expense with a destination) still counts; (3) hide the Category control on the card payment form (LED-146 Backlog) and show 12a's 'Excluded from spending reports' as static text. **Fallback:** none needed; behaviour is already as decided.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) OD-2 is answered and recorded (b); (b) isCardPayment is exported from src/lib/cardPayment.ts and unit-tested; (c) a test runs one fixture through buildCategoryBreakdown, summarizeRange and entryBudgetImpact and shows a transfer into a credit card contributes 0 to spending while a loan repayment still counts, and a source check pins the database `type = 'expense'` filter in useBudgets and useOverspending and the expense filter in Home's top categories (utils.ts cannot be loaded by node); (d) the card payment form no longer shows a Category control and says the payment is excluded from spending reports; (e) the payment still appears in Activity and moves the card balance; (f) no migration; (g) lint, build and test pass.
